goal: The eco-protocol-library page is a reference page with no data entry: its report is its outline. Read through the gateway, it carries exactly its 6 headings in order (Protocol Library ... The shrinking island), and is intact -- no leaked value, no script error, nothing pushed sideways. Pressing the first Copy puts exactly one clipboard text on the clipboard: meadow-disturbance.eco whole, 14 lines from name: meadow disturbance study to expect: evenness(bloom) is uneven, with its 3 phases and 5 expectations, one of them deliberately wrong. The second Copy puts two-ponds.eco whole on the clipboard, 12 lines from name: two-pond floristic comparison to expect: turnover(pondA, pondB) is moderate, its 3 expectations the bands the entered counts sit in.

expect.output.payloads.0.text:
name: meadow disturbance study
keys: 100
seed: 42
window: 250

phase: graze   uniform 2000        # even grazing
phase: bloom   hot 2000 5 90        # 5 keys carry 90% of the traffic
phase: seasons churn 1500 55        # turnover: births and deaths

expect: evenness(graze) > 0.9
expect: hill1(bloom) < 20
expect: brayCurtis(graze, bloom) > 0.5
expect: evenness(bloom) > 0.9        # deliberately wrong → REFUTED
expect: evenness(bloom) is uneven

name: two-pond floristic comparison
seed: 7

data: pondA cattail=18 duckweed=44 frogbit=3 azolla=9 rush=6
data: pondB duckweed=51 azolla=2 lily=12 rush=6

note: sampled both ponds after two dry weeks
note(pondA): heavy duckweed mat on the north edge

expect: jaccard(pondA, pondB) <= 0.5     # under half the flora shared
expect: evenness(pondA) is moderate        # duckweed leads, 44 of 80, but four others hold their share
expect: turnover(pondA, pondB) is moderate  # shared duckweed and rush keep the mats closer than they look
